title: POST create without Idempotency-Key — network retry creates duplicate
expected_feedback: Standard (S2, nature [C], trigger T1 live — §8.1 makes an unstated policy a FAIL here): POST /orders creates a priced order (total 49.99), so a replay charges the customer twice — risk trigger T1 (money movement) makes retry safety binding here rather than merely recommended. Mobile clients retry constantly (network timeout, app backgrounded, user double-tap). Fix: accept an Idempotency-Key header; on the first request process normally and store the response keyed by scope (tenant + subject + method + path) plus the key; on a retry with the same key and same body return the cached response with X-Idempotent-Replayed: true; on the same key with a different body return 409 idempotency_conflict. Set the TTL from the maximum client retry window plus clock skew, not from a fixed 24h habit. Note the boundary: the nature of this rule does not change without the trigger — only its severity does. On an append-only endpoint with no external side effect (T1–T3 absent) the same missing policy is a WARN, and a documented "replays are harmless here" is a PASS.
violated_rule: Retry safety and write-conflict policy specified where risk triggers apply
